title: THE EASTERN TRIBES KEPT THEIR WORD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over, ready for battle, in front of the Israelites, as Moses had directed them. About forty thousand armed for battle crossed over before the Lord to the plains of Jericho for war. — Josh 4:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Remember the promise from chapter one? The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh had already received their land east of the Jordan. They could have stayed home. But they had promised to help their fellow Israelites conquer the land first, and here they are — crossing over, armed and ready, keeping their word.

This is faithfulness in action. It is one thing to make a promise; it is another to follow through when the cost is real, when it means leaving your own settled land and marching into battle for others. About forty thousand men crossed over to fight not for their own inheritance, which they already had, but for their brothers'. That is true covenant loyalty.

There is a challenge for us here. When God has already blessed us, do we still show up to serve others? It would have been easy for these tribes to say, "We have ours; let the rest sort themselves out." Instead they honoured their commitment and stood with their brothers.

The New Testament calls us to this same self-giving spirit: "look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others" (Phil 2:4). This is the mind of Christ, who, though He possessed all the riches of heaven, came down to fight our battle and secure our inheritance. Having received, we give. Having been helped, we help.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Now that God has blessed you, are you still willing to serve others' battles?
2. Is there a promise or commitment you need to follow through on, even at a cost?
3. How does the self-giving mind of Christ challenge your priorities?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me faithful to my commitments, even when it costs me. Give me the mind of Christ to serve others' interests, not only my own. Amen.
